newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE RAISES CO-OP BANK EQUITY REQUIREMENTS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE RAISES CO-OP BANK EQUITY REQUIREMENTS.

text.p: The Bank of Greece said on Thursday it raised minimum equity requirements for co-operative banks, in place since 1993.

"Minimum equity levels are revised to ensure funding for improvements in informatics infrastructure and risk management services rendered necessary following recent relaxation of regulations pertaining to co-op banking operations," it said in a statement.
The central bank also cited the need to strengthen the financial status of these institutions in view of intensifying competition.

Minimum equity requirements for co-op banks operating within the strict limits of their prefectures are doubled to 1.2 billion drachmas, while those with regional activities must raise their share capital by 25 percent to 2.5 billion drachmas, it said.
The 4.0 billion drachma minimum for co-op banks with nationwide activities or with branches in either Athens or Thessaloniki was not revised.

Co-op banks already in business or those that have applied to the central bank for an operating licence by July 9, 1997 are offered an extension until end-1998 to adjust their equity capital. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
